newsitem.title: UK: Lasmo leads oil sector rally as stg drops.
newsitem.headline: Lasmo leads oil sector rally as stg drops.

text.p: Shares in UK oil and oil exploration companies firmed on Tuesday, even as the broad market fell, bolstered by sterling's sharp depreciation against the dollar, analysts and traders said.
Sterling, down to a five-month low against the dollar after UK Prime Minister John Major confirmed that the election will be held on May 1, helped lift shares in LASMO Plc 5p to 256-1/2.

Revenues of oil companies are priced in dollars, but earnings are repatriated and then calculated in sterling, so a weaker pound against the dollar translates into higher gross earnings in sterling terms.
Shares in British Petroleum added 8-1/2p to 711-1/2, while shares in Shell Transport firmed 10p to 1093.

Credit Lyonnais Laing analyst Jurjen Lunshof said that in addition to a more favourable exchange rate, the sector was bolstered by perceptions that crude oil prices are bottoming out. Brent crude oil has fallen some 25 percent from its January highs.
"The market is looking at inventories and the perception is that we've seen the extent of the decline," he said.
Lunshof said that improvements in productivity and profit margins have buoyed BP and LASMO shares in particular. "Both look set to outpace the sector," he added.
Second-tier oil exploration shares have been firming amid rising production and ongoing bid speculation, dealers and analysts said.
Shares in British Borneo jumped 16p to 1452-1/2, while shares in JKX Oil & Gas added 13p to 46-1/2.
